Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed for both food quality and service. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|-----------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, optional tofu) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Baan Thai** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Thai Orchid** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell peppers, bamboo shoots)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Siam Square** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Kha Gai” (no chicken, optional tofu) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Thai House** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants are located on the same block (1225 W 18th St) in the West Loop, so you can easily walk between them if you want to try a few different dishes. They’re all within a short distance of each other, making it convenient to explore multiple options in one visit. ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai Food 1. **Ask for “no egg” and “no fish sauce.”** Many Thai dishes contain eggs or fish sauce by default. Requesting “no egg” and “no fish sauce” will make the dish vegetarian. 2. **Choose tofu or tempeh.** Tofu is a common protein substitute in Thai cuisine. Tempeh is also available at some places. 3. **Look for “vegetarian” or “vegan” labels.** Restaurants often have a dedicated vegetarian menu or at least a few vegetarian options listed. 4. **Check the “vegetarian” section on the menu.** Most of these restaurants have a separate vegetarian section that lists all the dishes that are already vegetarian. 5. **Ask the server for recommendations.** Servers usually know which dishes are vegetarian-friendly and can suggest the best options. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more details (e.g., opening hours, reservation policies, or specific dish recommendations), just let me know.
